plan: This auction structure mirrors a second-price sealed-bid auction: the winner pays the second-highest bid, and my "exit price" in Stage 2 is simply my own sealed bid. Since I exit exactly at my bid regardless of others' bids, and I only pay the second-highest bid if I win, bidding my true value is a weakly dominant strategy. Bidding higher risks winning at a price above my value; bidding lower risks losing profitable opportunities. Therefore, I will bid exactly my value of $32.

This auction structure functions as a second-price auction: I exit at my sealed bid, and the winner pays the second-highest bid. In second-price auctions, bidding one's true value is the dominant strategy, as it maximizes expected profit regardless of others' bids. My value is $6, so bidding $6 ensures I win only when profitable (paying less than my value) and avoid overpaying. There's no incentive to shade or inflate my bid.

Since this is effectively a second-price auction (winner pays the second-highest bid), the dominant strategy is to bid exactly my true value. Bidding higher risks winning at a price above my value (negative profit), while bidding lower risks losing profitable opportunities. Bidding my value of $17 ensures I only win when it's profitable and pay a fair price determined by others' bids.
